Hi Claire —

Hope you're well. As we approach the end of your current term (Dec 31), I'd like to lock a 60‑minute QBR to align on:

- proposed new term (18 months vs 12) and pricing impact
- capacity uplift plan to hit your projected peak in H1
- staffing & escalation contacts for go‑live week
- procurement / legal next steps and calendar of deliverables

Can you do one of these windows next week for the QBR?
- Tue 11/17 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed 11/18 13:00–14:00 PT
- Fri 11/20 11:00–12:00 PT

If you prefer, I can invite procurement/finance and we can include a short runbook review (15m) at the end. I attached a short SOW draft and last 30‑day usage export so you and your finance team can see the uplift baseline.

Thanks — quick next step would be to lock a time so we can pull engineering/CS and legal into the agenda.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0129

Jasmine / Marissa —

Quick notes after a first pass on the usage export:
- baseline 30d burst + KV cache footprint suggests AtlasPay will need a +35% vCPU/GPU headroom in peak months if they keep current request patterns. I recommend we propose a two‑tier uplift: 1) immediate +25% reserved capacity and 2) optional +10% burst pool for marketing spikes.
- for post‑deploy oncall: propose lead CS (Rafael Mendes) + backup (Monica Patel) with an escalation matrix into SRE for platform incidents. I can put together a one‑pager runbook with contact phone/pager and 15m rollback steps by Mon 11/16.

I'll draft the runbook and include sample RTO/RPO commitments we can reasonably support within Dedicated reservations.

—Rafael
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Term transition & staffing checklist — locking QBR window

All —

Pricing thoughts (high level):
- Option A (12 months): standard uplift pricing + 10% volume discount after committed threshold of 180M tokens / mo. Shorter term, higher monthly ARR.
- Option B (18 months): 8% lower effective unit price with the same thresholds; include 2 months of service credit held for SLA exceptions.

Procurement asks we should address in SOW:
- explicit payment schedule (monthly vs net30 vs milestone invoicing)
- early‑termination calculation (pro‑rata minus credits)
- a single seat pricing and an uplift path for embeddings that are priced per 1k vectors

I recommend we prepare a 1‑page comparison sheet for the QBR (Marissa will own). I can have the draft comparison + payment term language by COB 11/15.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
